# `Q-5-12` — Project render scripts unsupported in this environment

> The environment cannot run subprocesses, so `project.pre-render` /
> `project.post-render` scripts were skipped.

## What this means

Your project configures render scripts, and this environment cannot
run them. The browser-based hub preview runs Quarto compiled to
WebAssembly, inside a sandbox with no process model — there is no way
to launch Python, R, or a shell from it.

Quarto skips the scripts and renders anyway, so you still get a
preview. What that preview lacks is whatever the scripts would have
produced: fetched data, generated pages, a rebuilt index.

This is a statement about where the render is happening, not a problem
with your configuration. The same project renders with its scripts on
a normal machine.

## Why this happens

- **Previewing a project in Quarto Hub** whose `_quarto.yml` declares
  render scripts.
- **A project shared from a machine where the scripts run**, opened in
  the browser preview by a collaborator.

## How to fix

Nothing needs fixing for the preview to work. To get the effects of
the scripts, render on a machine that can run them:

```bash
quarto render
```

Two ways to keep the browser preview useful in the meantime:

**Commit the generated artifacts.** If a pre-render script generates
files that change rarely, checking them in means the preview sees the
same inputs a full render would.

**Make the scripts optional.** If the generated content is
supplementary, the preview showing the document without it is a
reasonable degradation — which is what already happens here.
